events.title: Freshie Orientation Night
events.description:
Your first night as part of the guild. We run through what UPCSG actually does across a school year - the academic support, the competitions we send teams to, the socials, and the committees you can join - then get out of the way so you can meet the people you'll be spending the next four years with.

The second half is games and giveaways. Bring nothing but yourself; we'll handle the rest. Merch samples will be out on a table near the entrance if you want to check sizing before the pre-order window opens later this month.

Open to all incoming Computer Science freshies. Upperclassmen are welcome to drop in, and honestly we'd rather you did - the orientation goes better when there are people around who've already been through it.

events.title: CodeSprint: Intro to Competitive Programming
events.description:
A hands-on introduction to algorithmic problem solving, aimed at people who have never touched a contest problem before. We start from reading a problem statement properly and work up through complexity, greedy reasoning, and binary search.

Bring a laptop. Any language with a working compiler or interpreter is fine - the ideas transfer, and nobody is going to tell you your choice of language is wrong.

No prerequisites beyond an introductory programming course. If you can write a loop and an array, you have enough to follow along.

events.title: General Assembly
events.description:
The monthly org-wide meeting. ExeCom reports on what's moved since the last GA, each committee gives a short update, and then the floor opens.

The open forum is the part that matters. If you have a question about how something is being run, where the funds went, or why a decision was made, this is the venue for it - and it's on the record.

events.title: Merch Drop: Cosmic Hoodie Pre-orders
events.description:
The pre-order window for the 2026-2027 Cosmic Hoodie opens. Sizing samples will be on site, so come try one on before you commit to a size.

Pre-orders go through the guild store on this site: add the hoodie to your cart, check out, then send your GCash reference. An officer verifies the payment and your order moves to confirmed.

events.title: Industry Night: Tech Talks
events.description:
Alumni and industry partners talk about what the first year out of university actually looks like - the parts nobody puts in a job posting.

Expect frank answers on interviews, what a junior role really involves day to day, and which of the things you're learning now turn out to matter. Bring questions; the Q&A usually runs longer than the talks.

achievements.title: First Runner-Up, NEXT LEVEL: Esports Game Dev Challenge
achievements.description:
Second-year Computer Science students from UP Cebu earned top finishes at the NEXT LEVEL: Esports Game Dev Challenge

Team <blank> claimed first runner-up, and Team Casa de Kirby finished in the top ten during the 2026 Regional Science, Technology, and Innovation Week celebration organized by DOST Central Visayas, held on July 13-15, 2026, at Waterfront Cebu City Hotel.
Team <blank> developed the game SARAP!, a Filipino cooking game where players prepare nearly forgotten regional dishes. The team is composed of Tyrone Gareth Cular, Krysta Belle Amojedo, Alynnah Rhein Cahutay, and Clandestine Maglasang, mentored by Ms. J Isle Rocamora.
Another finalist, Team Casa de Kirby, created Rescue Rush, a speedrun game where players save civilians scattered around a flooded village as fast as they can. The team is composed of Resha Alpuerto, Angelo Luize Ramirez, Sam Joash Recodo, Joy Montilde, and John Kirby Monleon, under the mentorship of Mr. Eli Edrian Tan.

achievements.title: Two Teams Through to ICPC Regionals
achievements.description:
Two guild teams advanced past the regional qualifiers of the ICPC, the first time UPCSG has sent more than one team through in the same year.

Preparation started in June with weekly practice contests. The format was deliberately unglamorous - sit down, five hours, no phones, upsolve everything you missed the following week. Attendance held through the semester, which is the part that surprised the coaches.

Neither team placed in the regional finals. Both said afterwards that the qualifier itself felt easier than the practice sets, which is roughly the point.

achievements.title: Undergraduate Research Accepted at National Congress
achievements.description:
A guilder's undergraduate thesis on low-bandwidth mesh networking was accepted for presentation at a national computing research congress.

The work started as a course project about keeping messages moving when infrastructure goes down - a problem the Visayas has more practical experience with than most. It grew into a full thesis over two semesters.

The guild's role here was small and worth naming honestly: a room to practise the talk in, and five people willing to sit through it twice and ask hard questions.

achievements.title: Outstanding Student Organization, College of Science
achievements.description:
UPCSG was named Outstanding Student Organization for the College of Science, recognising org performance, member programs, and community engagement across the year.

The citation pointed at consistency rather than any single event: tutoring sessions that ran every week instead of only before finals, and a committee structure that kept working after the officers who built it graduated.

Awards like this belong to the year, not the ExeCom. Everyone who showed up to run a session, staff a booth, or answer a question in the group chat is part of why it landed.

achievements.title: First UPCSG Developers' Conference
achievements.description:
The guild ran its first full-day developers' conference on campus, drawing just over two hundred attendees from four schools.

Six talks, two workshops, and a hallway track that ran longer than any of them. Speakers came from local studios and from alumni two or three years out - close enough to the audience that the advice stayed concrete.

Running it taught the org more about logistics than any committee meeting had. The retrospective document is three pages long and is now required reading for whoever runs the next one.
